title: Coherent canonical modules, finite adjunction, and proper surface traces
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian normal local domain of dimension $2$ and let $W$ be a finite $A$-module such that $W[2]$ is a normalized algebraic dualizing complex [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], [def-per-algebraic-normalized-dualizing]. Work with ordinary Zariski $\mathcal O$-modules and their derived categories [def-pc-derived-category], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For every proper dominant generically finite morphism $a:Z\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $Z$ normal integral of dimension $2$, the complex $a^!(W[2])$ is $\omega_Z[2]$ for a coherent torsion-free module $\omega_Z$; $a^!$ here is the right adjoint of $Ra_*$ on derived quasi-coherent modules. These are the canonical modules normalized relative to $W[2]$ [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [pqf-def-coherent]. For a proper dominant generically finite morphism $h:Z\to Z'$ over $A$ between such schemes, the adjunction counit gives $\tau_h:h_*\omega_Z\to\omega_{Z'}$. The traces restrict to opens, satisfy $\tau_{h_2h_1}=\tau_{h_2}\circ(h_2)_*\tau_{h_1}$, and are the identity over any open on which $h$ is an isomorphism. If $h$ is finite, then $h_*\omega_Z=\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_{Z'}}(h_*\mathcal O_Z,\omega_{Z'})$, $\tau_h$ is evaluation at $1$, and for every coherent $\mathcal O_Z$-module $M$ there is a natural bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_Z(M,\omega_Z)=\operatorname{Hom}_{Z'}(h_*M,\omega_{Z'})$ given by composition with $\tau_h$. In particular, for a finite normal local extension $A\subset B$ of dimension $2$, $\omega_B=\operatorname{Hom}_A(B,W)$ is finite and $\omega_B[2]$ is normalized dualizing. A map of modules into any $\omega_Z$ is determined by its generic restriction. If $A$ is regular local of dimension $2$, any free rank-one $W$ makes $W[2]$ normalized dualizing, and $\omega_Z$ is invertible whenever $Z$ is regular.
